elements.requirement: Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the Tribunal has a duty to hear and determine any proceedings brought before them by virtue of section 65(2)(a) or (d).
elements.quote: it shall be the duty of the Tribunal— (a) to hear and determine any proceedings brought before them by virtue of section 65(2)(a) or (d)

elements.requirement: Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the Tribunal has a duty to consider and determine any complaint or reference made to them by virtue of section 65(2)(b), (ba) or (c).
elements.quote: it shall be the duty of the Tribunal— (b) to consider and determine any complaint or reference made to them by virtue of section 65(2)(b) , (ba) or (c)

elements.requirement: When hearing any proceedings brought by virtue of section 65(2)(a), the Tribunal must apply the same principles for making their determination as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review.
elements.quote: they shall apply the same principles for making their determination in those proceedings as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review

elements.requirement: When considering a complaint made by virtue of section 65(2)(b), the Tribunal has a duty to investigate whether the persons against whom allegations are made have engaged in conduct falling within section 65(5) in relation to the complainant, any of his property, any communications sent by, to, or intended for him, or his use of any postal service, telecommunications service or telecommunication system.
elements.quote: to investigate whether the persons against whom any allegations are made in the complaint have engaged in relation to— (i) the complainant, (ii) any of his property, (iii) any communications sent by or to him, or intended for him, or (iv) his use of any postal service, telecommunications service or telecommunication system, in any conduct falling within section 65(5)

elements.requirement: When considering a complaint made by virtue of section 65(2)(b), the Tribunal has a duty to investigate the authority, if any, for any conduct falling within section 65(5) that they find has been engaged in.
elements.quote: to investigate the authority (if any) for any conduct falling within section 65(5) which they find has been so engaged in

elements.requirement: When considering a complaint made by virtue of section 65(2)(b), the Tribunal has a duty to determine the complaint in relation to their investigative findings by applying the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review.
elements.quote: in relation to the Tribunal’s findings from their investigations, to determine the complaint by applying the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review

elements.requirement: The Tribunal is not under any duty to hear, consider or determine any proceedings, complaint or reference if it appears to them that bringing the proceedings or making the complaint or reference is frivolous or vexatious.
elements.quote: The Tribunal shall not be under any duty to hear, consider or determine any proceedings, complaint or reference if it appears to them that the bringing of the proceedings or the making of the complaint or reference is frivolous or vexatious

elements.requirement: Except where the Tribunal are satisfied, having regard to all the circumstances, that it is equitable to do so, they must not consider or determine any complaint made by virtue of section 65(2)(b) if it is made more than one year after the taking place of the conduct to which it relates.
elements.quote: Except where the Tribunal, having regard to all the circumstances, are satisfied that it is equitable to do so, they shall not consider or determine any complaint made by virtue of (a) section 65(2)(b) if it is made more than one year after the taking place of the conduct to which it relates

elements.requirement: Except where the Tribunal are satisfied, having regard to all the circumstances, that it is equitable to do so, they must not consider or determine any complaint made by virtue of section 65(2)(ba) if it is made more than one year after the personal data breach to which it relates.
elements.quote: Except where the Tribunal, having regard to all the circumstances, are satisfied that it is equitable to do so, they shall not consider or determine any complaint made by virtue of (b) section 65(2)(ba) if it is made more than one year after the personal data breach to which it relates

elements.requirement: Subject to any provision made by rules under section 69, the Tribunal have the power to make such interim orders pending their final determination as they think fit where any proceedings have been brought before them or any complaint or reference has been made to them.
elements.quote: Subject to any provision made by rules under section 69, where any proceedings have been brought before the Tribunal or any complaint or reference has been made to the Tribunal, they shall have power to make such interim orders, pending their final determination, as they think fit

elements.requirement: Subject to any provision made by rules under section 69, on determining any proceedings, complaint or reference, the Tribunal have the power to make any award of compensation or other order as they think fit.
elements.quote: Subject to any provision made by rules under section 69, the Tribunal on determining any proceedings, complaint or reference shall have power to make any such award of compensation or other order as they think fit

elements.requirement: Without prejudice to the power to make rules under section 69(2)(h), orders that may be made by the Tribunal include an order quashing or cancelling any warrant or authorisation.
elements.quote: the other orders that may be made by the Tribunal include— (a) an order quashing or cancelling any warrant or authorisation

elements.requirement: Without prejudice to the power to make rules under section 69(2)(h), orders that may be made by the Tribunal include an order quashing or cancelling a notice under Part 3 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 or a retention notice under Part 4 of that Act.
elements.quote: an order quashing or cancelling a notice under Part 3 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 or a retention notice under Part 4 of that Act

elements.requirement: Without prejudice to the power to make rules under section 69(2)(h), orders that may be made by the Tribunal include an order quashing or revoking a direction under section 225 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.
elements.quote: an order quashing or revoking a direction under section 225 of that Act

elements.requirement: Without prejudice to the power to make rules under section 69(2)(h), orders that may be made by the Tribunal include an order quashing or revoking a notice under section 252, 253 or 258A of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.
elements.quote: an order quashing or revoking a notice under section 252 , 253 or 258A of that Act

elements.requirement: Without prejudice to the power to make rules under section 69(2)(h), orders that may be made by the Tribunal include an order quashing an order under section 23A or 32A section 75 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 or section 32A of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 by the relevant judicial authority (within the meaning of that section).
elements.quote: an order quashing an order under section 23A or 32A section 75 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 or section 32A of this Act by the relevant judicial authority (within the meaning of that section)

elements.requirement: Without prejudice to the power to make rules under section 69(2)(h), orders that may be made by the Tribunal include an order requiring the destruction of any records of information that have been obtained in exercise of any power conferred by a warrant or authorisation or by a notice under Part 3 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, or that are held by any public authority in relation to any person.
elements.quote: an order requiring the destruction of any records of information which— (i) has been obtained in exercise of any power conferred by a warrant or authorisation or by a notice under Part 3 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016 ; or (ii) is held by any public authority in relation to any person

elements.requirement: Except as provided by virtue of section 67A, determinations, awards, orders and other decisions of the Tribunal (including decisions as to whether they have jurisdiction) are not subject to appeal or liable to be questioned in any court.
elements.quote: Except as provided by virtue of section 67A, determinations, awards, orders and other decisions of the Tribunal (including decisions as to whether they have jurisdiction) shall not be subject to appeal or be liable to be questioned in any court
